feature: Segmented control: our rail with a tinted glass chip
summary: Every row of side-by-side choices is our own control again: a solid grey rail, and the picked choice on a Liquid Glass chip tinted with your accent, its word in white. On a new pick the chip stretches across to the new choice and settles, and every word reads at 4.5:1 or better in every state.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording for View | Edit and the video panel; pick a text layer for Across and Down; press Shift-Cmd-H for the history bar.

try.do: Open a recording and press Cmd-2, then Cmd-1: watch the chip on View | Edit in the title bar.
Pick a text layer and click Center, then Right, in the Across row of the Text section.
Press Shift-Cmd-H and click Screenshots, then Videos, then All in the history bar.
Switch the Mac to Light, then Dark, and look at the Across and Down rows.
Look at the title bar's View | Edit in Light and in Dark.
Look at the history bar's filter in Dark.
Grab the chip in any row and drag it along the rail, then let go.

evaluate: Is this the tinted glass chip you pictured, or should the glass show more (the accent is laid over the glass so a white word always reads)?
Does the stretch as the chip travels read as liquid glass, or is it too quick to notice at about a third of a second?
Is the white word on the picked chip, and every grey word on the rail, easy to read everywhere you use the app?
Does the solid rail sit well in the title bar and over screenshots in the history bar?
rough: Tinted glass on its own could not hold a white word: measured in the app, it veiled the chip to #B0CCE0 (regular glass) and #7B92BA (clear glass) in light, where white reads 1.6:1 and 3.3:1. So the accent is laid over the glass at 88% and the glass shows at the chip's rim and a little through. Measured on the real window, white on the chip reads 5.4:1 in light and 7.2:1 in dark in all three places.
The chip is a deeper shade of your accent, not the accent itself: white on the Mac's own blue is 4.0:1.
The chip does not swell under a press the way interactive glass does: that swell drew 1.5pt past the chip and past any clip, so the pressed segment shrinks to 97% instead.
The chip moves on eased curves rather than a spring: the no-bounce spring was filmed carrying it 5pt past the end of the rail before settling.
The component page's drawn specimen still shows the old grey plate, not the tinted chip: the page's words now describe the tinted chip, but its shared drawing was left as drawn.
The page asks for fill, edge and lift on the picked segment; the chip has fill and the glass rim for an edge, and no drop shadow.
